svg.title: Photosynthesis & limiting factors
svg.desc: The reaction: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ Chlorophyll absorbs light; energy transfers from the environment to chloroplasts. Endothermic. CO₂ enters stomata; roots/xylem supply water. Light is energy, not a material reactant. Glucose pathways: Respiration releases energy; starch and fats/oils store resources. Cellulose strengthens cell walls. Glucose and nitrate ions supply materials for amino acids → proteins. Four interacting factors: More light or CO₂ raises rate only while that factor limits it. Warming towards optimum raises enzyme activity; excess heat can denature enzymes. Less chlorophyll → less light absorption. Magnesium deficiency or disease can reduce chlorophyll. Interpret the plateau: Rising rate with light → light is limiting. Plateau → another factor limits rate. Compare curves at the same other conditions: if added CO₂ raises rate, CO₂ had limited it. A plateau alone does not identify which factor limits rate. Inverse-square law: Intensity ∝ 1/distance². I₂/I₁ = (d₁/d₂)². 20 → 40 cm: intensity becomes ¼. 30 → 15 cm: becomes 4×. Use consistent units. Photosynthesis rate need not change by the same factor. Greenhouse decisions: Adding heat, light or CO₂ costs money. Improve the actual limiting factor. Extra profit = extra crop income − extra cost. £240 − £170 = £70. Highest photosynthesis rate is not always the most profitable setting.
